question: A 48-year-old man comes to the physician because of worsening shortness of breath and nocturnal cough for the past 2 weeks. On two occasions, his cough was bloody. He had a heart condition as a child that was treated with antibiotics. He emigrated to the US from Kazakhstan 15 years ago. Pulmonary examination shows crackles at both lung bases. Cardiac examination is shown. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
analysis: The most likely diagnosis for this patient with worsening shortness of breath, nocturnal cough with bloody episodes, and crackles at both lung bases is mitral valve stenosis. The history of a heart condition in childhood, emigration from Kazakhstan, and physical examination findings point towards this diagnosis.
